summary: Akio Tanabe works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–2006). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1993), Kyoto University (1998, 2004), and the University of Tokyo (professor in 2015).

Akira Fujieda studied at Kyoto University (~1931–1934), specializing in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He held appointments at Kyoto University (1937, 1948, professor in 1968), Copenhagen (1970), and UC Berkeley (1988), and taught Daishun Ueyama and Bruce Charles Williams.
Akira Hataya is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held an associate professorship at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and served as professor emeritus at Otani University (attested 2014).

Akira Hirakawa specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo (1939–1941, ~1954–1959) under Shoson Miyamoto. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1962–1975), Waseda University (1975–1985), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (1996).

Akira Miyaji specializes in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Nagoya University (~1964–1991), where he later became emeritus professor (~1974–2007). He also held posts at Hirosaki University, Shizuoka Prefectural Museum of Art, and Ryukoku University.
Akira Momiyama is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1972–1976) and served as a professor at Saitama University (attested 2005).

Akira Mukai works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Hokkaido University, where he was an assistant (attested 1978), and later became a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

Akira Omine worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kyoshi Takahama and at Kyoto and Heidelberg Universities. He held posts at Kyoto University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University (1980–1992), and Ryukoku University (1992).

Akira Sadakata works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, and at the University of Paris. He served as associate professor, professor, and professor emeritus at Tokai University (~1970–2007).

Akira Saito studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and earned his PhD at the Australian National University. A specialist in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, he held professorships at the University of Tokyo, Tokyo Medical University, and ICPBS.

Akira Shimada specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, under Rajeev Lochan and earned his PhD at SOAS under Daud Ali. He became an associate professor at SUNY New Paltz in 2007.

Akira Suganuma was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Toyo University (~1959–1962). He held posts as an assistant and associate professor at Toyo University (1962–1994) and lectured at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1981).

Akira Takeda was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (1949–1959) under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He taught at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (~1965–1983) and served as assistant and professor at the University of Tokyo (1961–1991).
Akira Yamada was a philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1943–1946) under Tokuryu Yamauchi and later held a post at Nanzan University (~1959–1967).

Akira Yuyama worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Akira Hirakawa, Naoshiro Tsuji, J.W. de Jong, and A.L. Basham, earning a PhD from ANU. He held posts at ANU, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Soka University.

Akitoshi Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He served as professor (attested 1982) and professor emeritus (attested 2014) at Taisho University, and as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).
Akong Tulku Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1967, he founded Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre, where he also served as abbot (attested 2009).
Akshara Ravishankar Parmeswaran works in Indology and philosophy. As of 2026, Parmeswaran is a doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago and a researcher at Ghent University.
Akshay Ramanlal Desai was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Mumbai (~1937–1946) under the supervision of Govind Sadashiv Ghurye (~1941–1946).

Alain Daniélou was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at St. John's College and Banaras Hindu University. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, the French Institute of Pondicherry, the Adyar Library, and founded comparative music institutes in Berlin and Venice.
